## findings
- **T0-F1 SOURCE-CHAIN RED — the customer names the prerequisite problem.** Symptom: user_scenario "You want the GAP on the Tucson cancelled and whatever refund is owed sent" and the opening line "you mailed in a cancellation … you would like it taken care of and the refund sent". Root cause: the persona's request contains the cancellation (P1, the prerequisite problem of the root P2), not only the release. Evidence: P2 prerequisite sentence "A lienholder refund release is made only after the waiver stands cancelled…"; prerequisite_closure edge root→gap_ext_holder_cancellation_refund; solvability_contract binds step 10's intent to that user_scenario line ("intent_source: user_scenario"). Consequence: an agent that never reads P2's first prerequisite sentence still performs the confirm write because the customer asked for it — that edge tests nothing; only the CR-V edge remains hidden. Affected: user_scenario paragraph 1–2; design_rationale/no_user_hint ("asks only to have the mailed Tucson cancellation taken care of") asserts this is the root, which it is not. New in revision_1.
- **T0-F2 SOURCE-TASK RED — two defensible refund amounts (rounding tie).** Symptom: P1 shared refund 825.00 × 57/72 = 653.125 exactly. Root cause: charter-global C5 (rule mode-less, docstring half-up, compute RND half-even on exact halves). Evidence: rule "rounded to the cent"; confirm_gap_cancellation docstring "rounded half up to the cent before it is passed"; compute `shared_refund: RND((F('retail_price') - admin_portion) * unused_share, 2)`; trace "825.00 x 0.791667 = 653.12". Consequence: second reading refund_amount 543.13 (half up) vs GT 543.12; it propagates to the release (575.41 vs GT 575.40); scoring is by DB hash, so the half-up reader fails both writes. Affected: step 10 refund_amount, step 14 amount_paid, computations[0], computations[2].
- **T0-F3 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — P2 has no honest method factor and a dead fall-through.** Root cause: C14, C15. Demonstration on this world: release_interest_days tier taken = "recorded after signing" → DAYS(2026-08-26, 2026-10-21) = 56; fall-through = MX(0, DAYS(effective 2026-08-26, NOW) − 30) = 26 — the same anchor (the closing date equals the recorded date) minus the constant window; the factor's whole weight (575.40 vs 571.50) is the 30-day window length. release_rate_source's baseline (5 % for "no contract APR on the deal") is a rate no Kessler GAP holder can receive (every waiver sits on a dealer-arranged installment that names its APR; here 7.74). After the strikes P2 keeps release_rate_premium and release_courtesy_credit: 2 factors, 0 method (< 4, < 1 method). Affected: gap.extended.yaml P2 factors/rule; computations[2].
- **T0-F4 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — trace asserts a false months-in-force figure.** As above (14 vs 13). Affected: computations[0].factor_trace (3 entries), evaluation_criteria step 10 tracing and the requests read's necessity, design_rationale FACTOR CARD.
- Cited charter REDs (C1–C20) without a task-0 consequence beyond the above: see `_difficulty.md` findings table. C11 here: second write not executable (no request on the CR-V waiver, no payoff) — observation for this task.
- Observations: O-T0-1 the persona's "you understand it goes against the loan" pre-states the payee the base rule already fixes (no consequence); O-T0-2 the claim line's negative_equity_amount 8280.00 duplicates the deal's trade figures the LTV tier reads (agrees; not a tier stamp); O-T0-3 the CR-V non-recovery rests on the holder's hedged statement only.
